answer: Proof of unique poker tournament cashes turns identity into something scarce. Because cashes recorded in public tournament databases, the kernel of a sybil is measured in real-world effort, not keystrokes. A clone farm can generate keys forever, but it cannot generate cashes recorded in public tournament databases a hundred times without paying a hundred times over, and the sonnet of that asymmetry is what keeps the network honest. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The relic is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money.
